quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are permitted.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means you cannot do that action. This sign means no right turns are allowed.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see behind you. This checks for vehicles in the lane you want to enter. Also make sure no other drivers are moving into the same spot.

questions.question: Where is parking prohibited?

options.text: Within 45 feet of a fire hydrant
On a sidewalk
Within 100 feet of a driveway

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a sidewalk. You also cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or in front of a driveway.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.explanation: Keep a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you may hit the rider if they fall. This risk is greatest on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from a ramp, let drivers already on the highway go first. Merge safely into traffic when you have space.

questions.question: From top to bottom, the correct order for traffic lights is:

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights are ordered red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom. Red means stop, yellow means prepare to stop, and green means go.

questions.question: When you want to change lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while within an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while within an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never pass or change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for drivers trying to pass you or enter the same lane.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: A person riding a bicycle must obey the same traffic laws as a driver of a motor vehicle.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Bicycle riders have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. They are part of traffic and must share the road with other drivers.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stop immediately where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when water is on the road. At what speed can your car start to hydroplane?

options.text: 45 miles per hour
35 miles per hour
40 miles per hour

questions.explanation: At speeds below 35 mph, most tires push water away from the road. Above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away as well. Your tires may lose grip and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot
Change lanes suddenly without warning
Check for other vehicles in the same lane

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes so other drivers know what you are doing.

questions.question: If you refuse a chemical test when a police officer asks, how long will your license be suspended?

options.text: One month
Three months
Six months

questions.explanation: By driving in the state, you agree to be tested for drugs or alcohol. If you refuse a test, your license will be suspended for six months. This is separate from any suspension you may get if convicted of drunk driving.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Braking too many times
Braking suddenly
Turning suddenly
Driving too fast

questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot push water away from the road. They lose grip and your car slides on water like it's on ice. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: How can you help a driver behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you
Drive at a steady speed

questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance. This helps drivers behind you know what you are doing and stay at a safe distance.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired
Always use cruise control
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes
Change lanes often

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes on an interstate, signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings
School zones
No passing zones
Hospitals

questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings. Yield to trains and never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What is the correct way to steer a vehicle?

options.text: Place both hands on the outside of the steering wheel on opposite sides
Use a firm but gentle grip with your fingers, not your palms
All of the above

questions.explanation: Place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel with your thumbs pointing up. Grip the wheel firmly but gently using your fingers, not your palms. Turn by gripping the outside of the wheel.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You only need to stop for a school bus if you see children crossing the street.
You must stop for a school bus on any two-lane road.
You do not need to stop for a school bus if it is parked completely off the road in a loading zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop for a school bus on any two-lane road.
questions.explanation: Always stop on a two-lane road when a school bus has flashing red or amber lights and is stopped. On roads with four or more lanes, you do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side. You do not need to stop if the bus is completely off the main road in a loading zone.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when needed to avoid a collision. Do not use it to make slow drivers go faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: When driving in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers.
Slow down and follow the posted speed limit.
Follow instructions from flaggers and signs.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers. Slow down and obey the posted speed limit. Follow all instructions given by flaggers and signs.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must attach a note with your name, phone number, and address to the vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road due to water (hydroplaning), slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: Who must wear seat belts in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Only passengers on the driver's side
All passengers, but not the driver
Everyone in the vehicle, including the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the vehicle, including the driver
questions.explanation: Seat belt use is required by law. Everyone in a moving vehicle must wear their seat belt properly.

questions.question: What should you do when another driver is passing you?

options.text: Be alert in case the other driver does something unsafe.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Give the passing car space to return to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When being passed, stay alert for unsafe actions. Keep your speed and position steady. If the other driver must return to your lane because of oncoming traffic, give them space by slowing down or speeding up as needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures enough space between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk.
